goal: Make the secure configuration msfslogger's default. Today every /api route is open to anyone who can reach port 3000, the server binds 0.0.0.0 in plaintext, and INGEST_TOKEN is optional (src/ingest.ts:120 — `if (!token) return true`). This run lands, exactly as frozen in design.md: a single-operator session login (scrypt over node:crypto, express-session over a better-sqlite3 store) gating every /api/* route except the three /api/auth endpoints and /api/ingest/*; TLS terminated inside the Node process with four fatal misconfiguration modes and no silent plaintext fallback; a mandatory INGEST_TOKEN with ALLOW_UNAUTHENTICATED_INGEST=1 as the documented opt-out and a timing-safe header comparison; explicit express.json and multer field/part limits; the puppeteer session-cookie forwarding that keeps PDF export working against its own gated API; the client login page, session hook and RequireAuth guard; and the README/agent/compose documentation an operator needs to get from a broken upgrade to a working deployment. It is a deliberate breaking change: an upgraded deployment that takes no action exits 1 with the exact messages of design §12.2 and §6.4. Out of scope, deliberately: multi-user, public-internet exposure, encryption at rest, ACME, audit logging, and any change to agent/agent.js, agent/traffic.js, client/vite.config.ts, client/src/components/Header.tsx, src/inspect-*.ts or tests/ existing files.
frozen_decisions: Web UI auth: session-based login (username/password -> server-side session cookie), gating all existing /api routes.
HTTPS: built into the Node server (TLS_CERT_FILE/TLS_KEY_FILE env vars), no silent plaintext fallback.
INGEST_TOKEN required by default; ALLOW_UNAUTHENTICATED_INGEST=1 is the documented opt-out.
Destructive ops (deletes, combine) get no extra step beyond the standard session gate.

Design-level freezes that follow from the above and are equally not open for redesign: one operator account stored in SQLite (not env), node:crypto scrypt N=16384 r=8 p=1 keylen=32 (no bcrypt/argon2 native addon), express-session@^1.19 as the only new runtime dependency, cookie name msfslogger.sid, one port serving one protocol with no HTTP->HTTPS redirect listener, and puppeteer page.setCookie (never setExtraHTTPHeaders) for the export loopback.
sequencing_rationale: COMMAND PREFIX — every command in every acceptance criterion runs under Node 20, i.e. is prefixed with: export NVM_DIR="$HOME/.nvm"; . "$NVM_DIR/nvm.sh"; nvm use 20 >/dev/null. The default node on this machine is v26 and better-sqlite3 has no binary for its ABI (.claude/ENVIRONMENT.md). Criteria name the bare command for readability; the prefix is never optional.

SCRATCH-SERVER RECIPE — src/db.ts:9 pins DB_PATH to path.join(process.cwd(), 'flights.db'), so a scratch server is made by changing cwd, never by editing db.ts. Every task that needs a running server uses exactly this, with its own port from the table below: SCRATCH=$(mktemp -d); cp /home/guilherme/msfslogger/flights.db /home/guilherme/msfslogger/flights.db-wal /home/guilherme/msfslogger/flights.db-shm "$SCRATCH/" 2>/dev/null; mkdir -p "$SCRATCH/client"; ln -s /home/guilherme/msfslogger/client/dist "$SCRATCH/client/dist"; cd "$SCRATCH" && PORT=<your port> ... node /home/guilherme/msfslogger/dist/index.js. Module resolution follows dist/'s own location, so better-sqlite3 and puppeteer resolve from the repo's node_modules regardless of cwd. Kill the server at the end of the task. Never bind 3000 and never open the repo's flights.db for writing.

SEAM 1 — src/server.ts is owned by exactly one task in this entire plan (T-007). Design §22 puts four separate concerns in that file (§8.3 middleware order, §8.5 body limits, §12.4 ingest wiring, §13.2 cookie forwarding at the two export routes); splitting them across tasks would break the one-file-one-Dispatcher rule, so they are one task. src/ingest.ts and src/pdfExport.ts join it because both change a signature that src/server.ts is the only caller of (createIngestRouter's third parameter, renderPdf's opts) — landing them separately would leave a tsc error between tasks.

SEAM 2 — Phase 1 gets the mandatory ingest token for free without touching src/server.ts. loadConfig() refuses to start when INGEST_TOKEN is unset and the opt-out is not set, and today's src/ingest.ts already enforces the header whenever process.env.INGEST_TOKEN is non-empty. So Phase 1 already delivers 'ingest is authenticated by default'; T-007's ingest change is only the config-threading and the timing-safe comparison. This is what lets the whole config/TLS/credential foundation ship before anything in src/server.ts moves.

SEAM 3 — the PDF-export cookie fix (design §13, R2, the highest-regression-risk item) is in the SAME task as the auth gate that breaks it, not a follow-up. T-007 cannot be reported done with a broken export; the phase-2 Reviewer re-renders a real PDF and compares page count and Content-Disposition against a pre-change capture.

SEAM 4 — client and server auth land in the same phase (phase 2), because a server whose UI cannot log in is not a shippable increment. T-008 (client) runs in parallel with T-006 (server auth modules) — client/src/** and src/** are disjoint — and verifies itself against a throwaway stub server in scratch that implements only /api/auth/* from contracts/samples/. The full-stack browser flow is the phase Reviewer's evidence.

PHASE GATE — the first task of each phase depends on the previous phase's reviewer task (T-006 and T-008 on T-005; T-010 on T-009). That gate is what stops T-004 (src/index.ts) and T-007 (src/server.ts) — which must agree about listener/config wiring — from ever running concurrently, and it stops T-010's README claims from being written against unreviewed behaviour.

TASK ORDER WITHIN PHASE 1 — T-002 and T-003 both depend on T-001 even though neither imports express-session. The reason is node_modules: T-001 runs npm install, and an agent running tsc or vitest against a node_modules being rewritten under it produces unreproducible failures. One extra serialization step is cheaper than one flaky review round.

NEW TEST FILES ONLY — design §19 item 5 forbids editing any existing file under tests/. Three new files are added, with disjoint names owned by one task each: tests/config.test.ts (T-002), tests/password.test.ts (T-003), tests/loginThrottle.test.ts (T-006). parseBooleanEnv, verifyPassword and LoginThrottle are the pure, high-consequence units in this run and are exactly what Vitest is good for; nothing that needs a server, a socket or flights.db goes into tests/.

EVERY task states the md5sum of /home/guilherme/msfslogger/flights.db before and after its work, and confirms the live server on port 3000 is still the same PID (ss -ltnp | grep :3000). The user's next restart of that server will hit the §20.1 refusal — that belongs in the final report to the user, and T-011 is the task that proves the documented recovery sequence works.

phases.name: Secure startup: configuration, schema, credentials, TLS listener
phases.ships: The server enforces its own security preconditions before it will run. A deployment with no INGEST_TOKEN exits 1 with the documented three-line message before the database is even opened; one with a token but no operator account exits 1 telling the operator to run `npm run set-password`; that CLI exists and creates the account against a live or stopped database. With TLS_CERT_FILE/TLS_KEY_FILE set the process serves HTTPS on one port, and every TLS misconfiguration is fatal rather than a quiet downgrade. Because today's ingest handler already enforces a non-empty INGEST_TOKEN, this phase alone closes the unauthenticated-ingest hole.

phases.name: The auth gate, the login API and the client login flow
phases.ships: The whole feature the user asked for, end to end: browsing to the app redirects to /login, a username and password create a session cookie, and every /api route answers 401 without one. Logout works, a mid-session expiry bounces the operator back to /login, cross-origin state-changing requests are rejected, ingest is token-authenticated with a timing-safe comparison, and PDF/KML export still produce the same files from inside a logged-in session.

phases.name: Documentation, packaging and the upgrade rehearsal
phases.ships: An operator who pulls this build and hits the exit-1 message finds the fix in README.md rather than in a stack trace: a First run section, the rewritten environment table, an HTTPS section with a working openssl one-liner, a named Insecure modes subsection, the verbatim upgrade sequence, and the dev note. agent/README.md tells the Windows side that INGEST_TOKEN is now required and how to trust a self-signed certificate; docker-compose.yml passes the new variables through. The whole sequence is then rehearsed against a copy of the live database.

tasks.title: src/index.ts — startup validation order, credential refusal, TLS/HTTP listener selection and the session sweep
tasks.goal: Rewire src/index.ts to the startup contract of design §7.3, §6.4, §11 and §10.5, without touching src/server.ts (createServer(flightManager) keeps its current signature this phase). tasks.title: Auth modules — SQLite session store, requireAuth/requireSameOrigin/LoginThrottle/sessionCookieFrom, and the /api/auth router
tasks.goal: Four new files under src/auth/ implementing design §9, §10.2, §13.2 and §16, none of them wired into the app yet (T-007 mounts them). (1) src/auth/express-session.d.ts — the SessionData augmentation from contracts/express-session.d.ts; this is the ONLY declaration of it anywhere in the tree (§4.4). (2) src/auth/sessionStore.ts — SqliteSessionStore extends session.Store with get/set/destroy/touch over the src/db.ts accessors; get treats a missing row, an expired row and a JSON.parse failure all as cb(null,null) and deletes the expired row; touch delegates to set; length and clear are not implemented; expiry is derived per §16.5 with the NaN fallback. (3) src/auth/middleware.ts — requireAuth (401 with the exact body of §8.2), requireSameOrigin (the five-step algorithm of §16.3, skipping GET/HEAD/OPTIONS, non-/api paths and /api/ingest/*), LoginThrottle (the fixed-window algorithm of §16.2 with WINDOW_MS 15 min, MAX_FAILURES 10, the window start that does not move, and the >1000-entry bounding), and sessionCookieFrom(req) which parses req.headers.cookie for msfslogger.sid and returns the value still percent-encoded (§13.2). (4) src/auth/routes.ts — createAuthRouter() with POST /login implementing §16.1 step by step (regenerate BEFORE setting req.session.user; one full scrypt derivation against DUMMY_PASSWORD_HASH on both no-user and wrong-user paths), POST /logout always 204 after destroy+clearCookie, GET /session always 200 with Cache-Control: no-store, and the log lines of §9.4 which never contain a password.
